name: Kadhi Pakora
description: Sour yogurt and gram flour simmered into a thick tangy gravy with fried besan fritters. It is common to Haryana and Punjab.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or paratha.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kadhi chawal' at a dhaba.

name: Bajra Khichdi
description: Khichdi made with pearl millet instead of rice, soaked overnight and cooked with moong dal and spices. It is a named dish of Haryanvi cuisine.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with ghee and buttermilk or yogurt.
how_to_order: Mostly home-cooked in winter; some rural dhabas serve it.

name: Murthal Paratha
description: Large stuffed parathas served with a slab of fresh white butter at the highway dhabas of Murthal on the Grand Trunk Road near Sonipat. The dhabas date from the 1950s, and the aloo paratha here is seen as the benchmark for North Indian highway parathas.
how_to_eat: Let the white butter melt into the layers and eat with yogurt, pickle and a glass of lassi.
how_to_order: Stop at a Murthal dhaba and ask for an 'aloo paratha with makhan'; go before 8 am to avoid queues.

name: Bajre ki Roti
description: Flatbread made from pearl millet (bajra) flour and eaten with ghee. It is one of the best-known breads of Haryana, a state that eats roti far more than rice.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with a generous spoon of ghee, a sabzi and buttermilk.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bajre ki roti' at a village-style dhaba, mostly in winter.

name: Singri ki Sabzi
description: Dried desert beans (singri, also ker sangri) soaked overnight, boiled and cooked with spices, amchur and sometimes yogurt into a thick curry. The dish is shared by Haryana and Rajasthan.
how_to_eat: Eat it with bajra roti, puri or paratha.
how_to_order: Ask for 'singri ki sabzi' at Haryanvi dhabas; dried singri is sold in markets.

name: Churma
description: Roti mashed with ghee and jaggery. In Haryana it is also eaten without ghee as a diet for wrestlers in the akharas.
how_to_eat: Eat it with a tall glass of warm milk, lassi or with kadhi.
how_to_order: Mostly home food; some dhabas serve it with a thali.

name: Gohana Jalebi
description: Giant jalebis fried in desi ghee, each weighing about 250 grams, from the town of Gohana. The style dates to 1958, when Matu Ram started selling them, reportedly piping batter through an earthen pot to get the thick rings.
how_to_eat: Break off a piece of the thick ring; one jalebi is enough to share.
how_to_order: Ask for a box by weight; a box of four (about 1 kg) costs around 320 rupees.

name: Lassi
description: A yogurt drink churned with water, served sweet or salted. Haryana's food relies heavily on dairy, and lassi is its favourite drink.
how_to_eat: Drink a tall glass with or after a meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'meethi' or 'namkeen lassi' at any dhaba or dairy.
